notes: Announced 2026-05-08. World's first dual-core neutral-atom quantum computer. 100 Rb-85 atoms (core 1) + 100 Rb-87 atoms (core 2) = 200 total physical qubits. Two cores operate in parallel (efficiency mode) or main+auxiliary (stability mode for logical qubits). Power consumption < 7 kW — no dilution refrigerator required. Standard cabinet form factor, deployable in ordinary indoor spaces. NO gate fidelity or benchmark results published — claim is architecture novelty, not performance. Context: Atom Computing demonstrated 1,180 qubits and 28 logical qubits (Bernstein-Vazirani, error-corrected) in 2024, well exceeding Hanyuan-2 in both metrics. DISPUTED ASPECTS: No independent verification; performance benchmarks absent. RELEVANCE TO OUR WORK: Low relevance. 200 physical qubits with no stated fidelity is not a useful target for MERA holographic circuits. Architecture novelty (dual-core) is interesting but no demonstrated gate-level operations reported.
